skill.name: reactome-database
skill.description: Query Reactome pathway data and run enrichment analysis through Reactome REST APIs for systems biology research.
skill.summary: Explore Reactome pathways, map genes to pathways, and run enrichment analysis from Claude-compatible workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Reactome research helper with clear external API use and no prompt injection or malicious intent found. Most static findings are false positives from markdown backticks, fixed documentation URLs, or API reference text. Real residual risks are third-party submission of biological identifiers to Reactome and a helper-script output file that can overwrite a local path derived from user input.

remediation.issue: Outbound network requests send pathway IDs, search terms, tokens, and gene lists to Reactome.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice before examples and helper-script usage, and advise users not to submit protected or unpublished biological data without approval.

remediation.issue: The helper script lacks request timeouts for Reactome API calls.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a reasonable timeout to each requests.get and requests.post call so commands do not hang indefinitely.

remediation.issue: The helper script writes results to a filename derived from the input gene file.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output path or ensure generated output never equals the input path before writing.

content.value_statement: Pathway analysis often requires switching between API docs, scripts, and browser tools. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for Reactome queries and enrichment workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Reactome Content Service and Analysis Service endpoints.
Shows how to query pathway entities, participating molecules, and database metadata.
Guides overrepresentation analysis for gene or protein identifier lists.
Documents expression data input formats for Reactome analysis submissions.
Includes a Python helper script for version, query, search, entity, and analysis commands.
Builds Reactome Pathway Browser links from returned analysis tokens.
limitations: Requires network access to public Reactome services for live API calls.
Analysis tokens and submitted identifiers are handled by Reactome, not by this skill.
The bundled helper script does not implement rate limiting or request timeouts.
The reactome2py package mentioned by the skill is noted as not actively maintained.

use_cases.title: Prioritize pathways from a gene list
use_cases.description: Run or plan overrepresentation analysis and interpret enriched pathway results with p-values and FDR values.

use_cases.title: Look up pathway context
use_cases.description: Query pathway identifiers, participating entities, species details, and related reaction metadata from Reactome.

use_cases.title: Prototype Reactome API workflows
use_cases.description: Use the examples and helper script to build repeatable API calls for research notebooks or pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Find a pathway by identifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome skill to explain what pathway R-HSA-69278 represents and what API endpoint retrieves it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan enrichment analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome skill to outline how I should run overrepresentation analysis for this gene list: TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare expression input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome skill to check whether my expression table format is suitable for Reactome Analysis Service and explain any fixes needed.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reusable workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome skill to design a Python workflow that submits identifiers, filters significant pathways by FDR, saves results, and creates a browser link.

output_examples.input: Analyze TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, and MYC with Reactome.
output: Recommended endpoint: Reactome Analysis Service identifiers submission.
Expected result: enriched pathways with matched entity counts, p-values, FDR values, and an analysis token.
Next step: review significant pathways and open the Pathway Browser link for the top result.
Recommended endpoint: Content Service event participatingPhysicalEntities.
Expected result: proteins, complexes, or small molecules associated with the pathway or reaction.
Note: validate the stable identifier before using returned entities in downstream analysis.

output_examples.input: Can I use mouse genes for human pathway projection?
output: Use the projection endpoint when mapping non-human identifiers to human pathways.
Confirm that identifiers are supported by Reactome before interpreting missing mappings.

best_practices: Confirm that submitted identifiers are not sensitive before sending them to Reactome services.
Reuse analysis tokens during their validity period to avoid duplicate submissions.
Filter enrichment results by FDR before drawing biological conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not submit protected or unpublished biological data without approval.
Do not treat example pathway IDs as results for your own dataset.
Do not run many individual requests when a batch endpoint can handle the same identifiers.

faq.question: Does this skill run Reactome locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses public Reactome REST APIs and documentation for live pathway queries and analysis.

faq.question: Can it analyze gene expression data?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the TSV format required by Reactome and how to submit the data to the Analysis Service.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python helper script for common Reactome API operations.

faq.question: Is network access required?
faq.answer: Yes. Live queries and analysis submissions require outbound HTTPS requests to Reactome.

faq.question: Can it visualize results?
faq.answer: It can construct Reactome Pathway Browser links from pathway IDs and analysis tokens.

faq.question: Does it replace biological review?
faq.answer: No. It helps retrieve and organize pathway data, but scientific interpretation still requires domain review.
